title: Weekend meal prep: 2 hours for 5 workdays of packed lunches
intro: With 2 hours on the weekend, you can prepare packed meals for almost a full work week. No need to cook like a chef, just one protein, one carb and some easy vegetables.

sections.p: Choose 2 types of protein, for example chicken and eggs. Choose 1-2 types of vegetables that last long, like cabbage, long beans or broccoli. List your items and shop just once at the market or supermarket.

Minute 0: cook rice and boil eggs. Minute 15: marinate the chicken and put it into the oven or air fryer. Minute 30: cut and stir-fry the vegetables. Minute 60: cook a second dish like tauhu masak kicap or sambal ikan bilis with less oil. Minute 90: divide into containers and wash the pots.

Use an easy guide: half the container vegetables, one quarter protein, one quarter rice. For most women, an estimated 3/4 to 1 cup of rice and a palm-sized portion of protein is suitable. One container like this is usually an estimated 400-500 kcal.
Keep Monday to Wednesday meals in the fridge. Thursday and Friday meals are better frozen and taken out the night before. Reheat until properly hot before eating.
Change the sauce every day: soy sauce, sambal, black pepper sauce or a little curry gravy. Same dish, different taste. Swap one type of protein every week so you don't get tired of it quickly.

action: Set a 2-hour slot on Sunday in your phone calendar.
Buy 5 containers of the same size so your portions stay consistent.
Start with 3 days of packed meals first, then increase to 5 days.
Boil 6-10 eggs at once for breakfast or snacks.
Take a photo of your meal prep every week as motivation.
myth: Many people think meal prep means eating plain boiled chicken and broccoli every day. Actually you can prep normal Malay, Chinese or Indian dishes, as long as the oil and portions are controlled.

faq.q: How many days can rice last in the fridge?
faq.a: Generally, cool rice quickly and keep it in the fridge for no more than 1-2 days. For the following days, freeze it and reheat it properly before eating.

faq.q: I don't have an oven, how?
faq.a: Use a wok or pot. Ayam masak kicap, ayam masak halia or ikan asam pedas are also suitable for meal prep. Just reduce the oil a little.

faq.q: What if I have lunch with my boss, what about my packed meal?
faq.a: Take it home and eat it for dinner. Or keep that container frozen and use it next week.
